title: The market already reads the standings
generated_utc_basis: 2026 decided games; strict prior-date team history
question: Does the closing line overprice teams whose records flatter their margins?
headline: Across 224 games, the market moved 0.72 points per record-gap unit while results moved 0.52; the supposed fade was already in the price.
body: We went looking for a market error and found a better story: closing lines already discount teams whose records run ahead of their scoring margins.
The close moved -0.72 points per gap unit; actual margin moved -0.52. Their difference, market error, was +0.20 (cluster z +0.61, wild-cluster p 0.544). That is not a usable fade.
This is a null, not proof of zero. The 80% power bound is about 2.8 points per one-standard-deviation gap; smaller effects can hide.
Every gap uses only games dated strictly before the game being tested. Closing prices grade the hypothesis; they are never model inputs.
